How this calculator works

Split a bill and calculate a tip per person. The calculation runs locally in your browser, so your entered values are not sent to a server.

Important note

Results are estimates for informational purposes. Check the assumptions and limitations shown with your result before making financial, medical or other important decisions.

Calculator guide

What is the Tip Calculator?

A tip calculator estimates gratuity and can split a bill evenly among a group. It is useful when checking a restaurant bill or deciding each person's share.

How does this calculator work?

The calculator multiplies the bill by the tip percentage, adds the tip to the bill and divides the total by the number of people.

Formula and calculation method

Tip = bill × tip percentage / 100. Total per person = (bill + tip) / number of people.

The calculator applies this method to the values entered above. Review the assumptions below before relying on an estimate.

Example calculation

For a bill of 85 and a 15% tip shared by two people, the tip is 12.75 and the total is 97.75, or 48.875 per person.

How to use the Tip

  1. Enter each requested value using the unit shown beside the field.
  2. Check the inputs and select Calculate result.
  3. Review the headline result, supporting metrics and chart where provided.
  4. Change one input at a time to compare scenarios, or use Reset to start again.

Tips for interpreting your result

  • Decide whether tax should be included in the tip base.
  • Enter the bill amount consistently.
  • Round each share according to the payment method.

Assumptions and limitations

The calculator splits the total evenly and does not support different orders, service charges, tax allocation or custom rounding.

Frequently asked questions

Does the tip apply before tax?

It applies to the bill amount entered; include tax in that amount if desired.

Can it split unevenly?

No, this version divides the total equally.

Does it round to cents?

Displayed values are formatted for readability; fractional minor units may remain in the calculation.
